text: {"domains":{"block_M":[64,128],"block_N":[64,128],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3],"threads":[128]},"shared_memory_limit":49152,"weights":{"traffic":1.0,"launches":0.5,"pipeline":0.5,"footprint":1.0},"rationale":"Problem is 4096x4096x1024 float16 GEMM with float32 accumulation. All block_M/block_N in {64,128} and block_K in {32,64} divide M=4096, N=4096, K=1024, so the full domain is feasible; threads fixed at 128 per allowed values. Shared memory estimate 2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, max at block_K=64, block_M=block_N=128, stages=3 is 2*64*256*3=98304 bytes, exceeding the cap, so the 49152-byte limit meaningfully prunes high-stage large-tile tuples while admitting e.g. 128x128x32x3 (49152) and 128x64x64x2 (49152). Traffic weight captures operand reload reduction from larger tiles; footprint weight penalizes shared-memory pressure; launches weight mild since 4096-wide outputs already give small launch counts; pipeline weight mild to favor deeper K blocking without overfitting to unmeasured behavior. These are analytic objectives only; no GPU timings, SASS, or correctness results are asserted, and CPU-shadow correctness would not establish CUDA correctness or GB10 performance."}
